question.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{2} & =4{c}_{1}-2{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{3} & =2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & a & 2 \\ b & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & c & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=4,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=-2.$
